L7@P0: MEDITERRANEAN CONVOY OPERATIONS.
L8@P0: OPERATION " EXCESS "
L9@P0: The following Despatch was submitted to the
L10@P0: Lords Commissioners of the Admiralty on
L11@P0: the igth March, 1941 by Admiral Sir Andrew
L12@P0: B. Cunningham, G.C.B., D.S.O., Commander-in-Chi'ef, Mediterranean Station.

L15@P0: OPERATIONS M.C.4 AND M.C.6
L16@P0: Be pleased to lay before Their Lordships the
L17@P0: enclosed reports on Operation M.C 4 (which included Operation " Excess ") and Operation
L18@P0: M.C.6,* carried out between 6th and i8th
L19@P0: January, 1941.
L20@P0: 2. These operations marked the advent of
L21@P0: the German Air Force in strength in the Mediterranean, and included the damaging of
L22@P0: H.M.S. ILLUSTRIOUS on loth January and
L23@P0: the loss of H.M.S. SOUTHAMPTON on nth
L24@P0: January.
L25@P0: 3. The incident reported in paragraph 7 of
L26@P0: Enclosure No. 6f illustrates the difficulty of
L27@P0: passage through the Narrows during periods
L28@P0: of bright moon when, in order to avoid the
L29@P0: known minefields, it is necessary to pass within
L30@P0: gun and visibility range of Pantellaria.

L38@P0: 4. With regard to the dawn action reported
L39@P0: in Enclosures Nos. 6 and 9,* it is thought that
L40@P0: this must have been a chance encounter, as
L41@P0: so small an Italian force would hardly have
L42@P0: been sent unsupported to attack a heavily
L43@P0: defended convoy. The heavy expenditure of
L44@P0: ammunition by BON A VENTURE, largely incurred in an effort to sink a crippled ship,
L45@P0: serves to emphasise the importance of using
L46@P0: the torpedo at close range on such occasions.
L47@P0: 5. I fully concur with the remarks of the
L48@P0: Vice-Admiral, Light Forcesf concerning the
L49@P0: towing of GALLANT by MOHAWK (Enclosure No. i if), and consider that this was a
L50@P0: most ably conducted operation.
L51@P0: It cannot be satisfactorily determined
L52@P0: whether GALLANT was mined or torpedoed,
L53@P0: but the absence of tracks and failure by the
L54@P0: enemy to claim her sinking lend probability
L55@P0: to the supposition that it was a mine.
L56@P0: 6. The dive bombing attacks by German aircraft were most efficiently performed and came
L57@P0: as an unpleasant surprise. The results of short
L58@P0: range A.A. fire were disappointing, though it
L59@P0: has been subsequently learned that this fire
L60@P0: was in fact more effective than dt appeared, and
L61@P0: the Germans suffered considerable loss.

L73@P1: Nevertheless, it is a potent new factor in
L74@P1: Mediterranean war and will undoubtedly deny

L80@P1: 7. The dive bombing attacks on the 3rd
L81@P1: Cruiser Squadron on the afternoon of nth
L82@P1: January—resulting in the loss of SOUTHAMPTON—were a complete surprise, delivered at
L83@P1: a time when the ships concerned believed themselves to have drawn clear of the threat of
L84@P1: air attack, and when officers and men were •
L85@P1: doubtless- relaxing their vigilance to some extent after a*very strenuous four days.
L86@P1: This damaging attack served to emphasise
L87@P1: the importance of including an R.D.F. ship*
L88@P1: in detached units whenever possible.
L89@P1: 8. The remarks of the Commanding Officer,
L90@P1: H.M.S. JAGUAR are of considerable interest,
L91@P1: in particular his practice of firing 4.7-mch barrage over the stern of a ship attacked by
L92@P1: dive bombers. The idea is now under development in the Mediterranean Fleet with a view
L93@P1: to the destroyer screen putting an " umbrella
L94@P1: barrage " over the fleet.
L95@P1: 9 Force X|' had originally put to sea to
L96@P1: take part in the offensive operations intended
L97@P1: in Operation M.C.6, which had to be abandoned It was most unfortunate that persistent bad weather prevented the RearAdmiral, ist Battle SquadronJ from delivering any of the attacks which he intended, and
L98@P1: which would have been a most useful counter
L99@P1: to the undoubted set back which the fleet
L100@P1: as a whole had received.
L101@P1: 10. It is satisfactory to record that Convoy
L102@P1: " Excess " whose safe passage had been the
L103@P1: main object-'of the operation, reached its
L104@P1: destination safely.
